original_test_intent: Use the BMC Immediate Shutdown control to cut host power abruptly, prove the intended SUT reaches and remains Off, and confirm it can later be recovered under the approved plan.
original_method: Bind the exact SUT/BMC and advertised Immediate/ForceOff semantics; stop all workloads, writes and storage activity; capture boot/filesystem/log state; issue one BMC Web Immediate Shutdown; observe the forced transition to stable Off with bounded BMC/console polling; retain evidence, then perform only the separately approved recovery power-on and assess filesystem/boot health.
manual_activity: The owner explicitly approves the power cut and proves all writes are stopped; an operator watches BMC/console/PDU recovery, authorizes the later power-on and owns the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC Web Immediate semantics and ForceOff mapping
Pre-cut boot ID and filesystem state
Expected Off-transition timeout and retention interval
Controlled power-on and filesystem/boot recovery plan
safety_requirements: Never ForceOff during active write, update, rebuild or critical workload
Use a protected validated session bound to one target
Do not label or evaluate the cut as orderly
Do not automatically retry after rejection or timeout
Observe stable Off before any power-on
Stop on wrong target, unexpected restart, BMC loss or unsafe recovery
Preserve unclean-shutdown/kernel/SEL evidence and do not clear logs
agent_execution_scope: Capture target and pre-cut workload/storage/filesystem baseline
Operate the literal Web Immediate Shutdown or approved equivalent once
Observe the forced transition and stable Off
Assist approved recovery checks and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve target, action mapping and destructive window
Confirm every write/storage operation is stopped
Define Off retention and recovery acceptance
Control recovery power-on and incident handling

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: ForceOff may map to Immediate Shutdown after advertised support and Web-equivalence approval, but a five-second wait plus `PowerState` neither proves the transition nor safe recovery; the orderly-risk phrase is incorrect.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the BMC Web Immediate Shutdown or accepted ForceOff equivalent once, with target-bound transition polling, stable-Off retention, preserved abrupt-cut artifacts and a separately authorized recovery boot.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Immediate mode, final Off state and 10/20-minute estimates are retained; no graceful-shutdown inference or repeated power command is added.

modernized_recommendation.status: ONE-SHOT FORCED POWER-OFF WITH CONTROLLED RECOVERY
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Link the approved action acknowledgement to console loss, BMC Off transition and an Off retention interval; only after evidence freeze, power on through the recovery plan and compare filesystem, boot and service health with the pre-cut baseline.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes forced behavior, data-integrity risk, stable terminal state and recovery measurable without weakening the immediate-shutdown objective.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A successful API response or final Off sample cannot establish correct target, transition timing or recoverability; WebUI coverage requires the literal path unless equivalence is approved.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: ForceOff can lose cached writes and damage filesystems even on an apparently idle host, and a management-controller fault can prevent the planned recovery.

project_override_considerations: The Project must approve ForceOff equivalence, the Off retention interval and recovery boot checks. Immediate Reboot must not substitute because it ends On; Orderly Shutdown must not substitute because it exercises OS cooperation.
expected_evidence: Verified target/action mapping, explicit destructive approval and complete workload/storage quiescence
Pre-cut boot ID, mount/filesystem/write activity, service and power baseline
Single Web Immediate Shutdown or approved ForceOff request/response
Timestamped console/power transition and stable PowerState Off before recovery
Approved recovery power-on, filesystem/boot/service comparison, incident record and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently specify an immediate shutdown. The orderly wording exists only in DeepSeek risk text and is rejected.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Action mapping, destructive approval, quiescence, Off oracle and recovery are normal owner-controlled inputs; the forced-power-off purpose is explicit.

review_improvement: Corrects the orderly mischaracterization and defines the source's immediate shutdown as a one-shot forced cut whose stable Off state and later recovery must both be evidenced.
independent_technical_reasoning: ForceOff deliberately removes power without OS shutdown, so clean-unmount evidence is not the expected mechanism. The safety question is whether all preventable writes were stopped and whether the exact target reached stable Off once. Recovery health must be assessed afterward because the destructive consequence can remain hidden until the next boot.
